BiblicalUsage: Zanun is adultery as a settled pattern, and the prophets use it for idolatry. In Genesis 38:24 Judah is told Tamar "hath played the harlot," and in 2 Kings 9:22 Jehu answers Joram, "What peace, so long as the whoredoms of thy mother Jezebel and her witchcrafts are so many?" Ezekiel 23:11 describes a sister "more corrupt in her inordinate love," and Hosea 1:2 opens the prophet's marriage with the charge that "the land hath committed great whoredom."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God uses this word because he will not call unfaithfulness by a softer name. I hold that Hosea 1:2 shows the whole land can commit whoredom against him, and that Jezebel's whoredoms in 2 Kings 9:22 were not private sins but a kingdom-wide corruption. My position is that zanun should make me guard my worship, because the heart that wanders from God always finds another lover.
